title: Page skein coalescer and stochastic prefill scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate and implement a 'page skein' coalescing layer plus a stochastic prefill admission/scheduler for paged attention KV caches. Goal is to reduce decode tail latency and reduce fragmentation from interleaved multi-tenant access while preserving throughput. This ticket bundles design, simulation, and a conservative incremental rollout for the runtime change that affects allocation, eviction, and prefill admission policy.
background: Current paged-attention behavior experiences frequent micro-fragmentation when concurrent requests interleave on shared KV shards. We see elevated 99th percentile decode latency under mixed short/long sequences and tenant contention. Existing eviction is LRU-like at page granularity; prefill is admitted synchronously which creates hotspots and decode stalls. Prior work covered slab compaction heuristics and kernel hints (see dependencies) but we need a lighter-weight coalescer and scheduling layer that can be deployed without a full compaction pass.
problem_statement: When multiple tenants/predictions touch overlapping token spans, small fragments accumulate across pages. Evicting single pages causes repeated re-prefill thrash. Prefill admission is greedy and does not consider scheduled decode waves, causing kernels to be starved or throttled and increasing tail latency. We need a policy that (1) coalesces near-adjacent fragments into resealable "skeins", (2) defers low-value prefill in favor of critical hotpaths, and (3) integrates kernel selection hints so compute placement matches residency.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a lightweight in-memory "page-skein" coalescer that tracks recent fragment touch ranges per shard. The coalescer will maintain soft groupings (skeins) of adjacent fragments and expose preferred coalescing candidates to the eviction controller. 2) Add a stochastic prefill scheduler: prefill requests are scored by expected reuse (based on touch frequency window, token-span length, tenant weight) and scheduled probabilistically into decode waves to smooth kernel load. 3) Surface kernel-hint metadata on skeins (e.g., stride characteristic, model-arch bucket) so the runtime can prefer kernel variants compatible with coalesced pages. 4) Conservative fallback: new coalescer runs in read-only simulation mode for N minutes, then opt-in for eviction hints, then enable admission gating behind a feature flag per cluster.
design_notes:
- Skein metadata: {start_token, end_token, last_touch_ts, touch_count, estimated_reuse_score, kernel_bucket}. Values stored in compact bloom-like buckets to keep per-shard memory low.
- Coalescer runs in background at configurable cadence (default 500ms).
- Stochastic scheduler uses an exponential backoff on repeated prefill failures and a tenant-weight-normalized score; admission probability = sigmoid(alpha * (score - threshold)).
- Eviction uses skein-aware soft-evict: if pages belong to the same skein, prefer evicting whole skein groups unless doing so would violate tenant isolation quotas.
- Kernel hinting: attach micro-metadata to skein to prefer microkernels that optimize for stride and kv-layout. This is advisory, not required.
perf_goals: Reduce 99th-percentile decode latency by >= 20% on mixed short/long workloads (internal mixed-traffic replay)
Reduce repeat prefill bytes moved by >= 30% for top-5 tenants in our replay set
No more than 3% regression in median throughput for batch workloads
acceptance_criteria: Skein coalescer runs in simulation mode without changing eviction for at least one cycle and produces candidate reports matching expected clusters
Stochastic prefill scheduler reduces peak kernel queue depth during replay tests compared to baseline
Feature-flagged rollout can enable/disable admission without impacting in-flight requests
Automated unit and integration tests cover skein merge/unmerge, scheduler admission probability, and fallback paths
observability: new dashboard panels show skein reuse rate, prefill admission rate, and kernel-hint mismatch rate
implementation_tasks: Design and proto: implement compact skein representation and coalescer simulation (Aisha)
Scheduler: implement stochastic admission logic and scoring function (Marco)
Eviction adaptor: add skein-aware soft-evict hints to existing eviction controller (Backend team)
Kernel integration: surface skein kernel_bucket metadata for kernel selector to consume (Runtime infra)
Tests: unit tests for skein merge edge cases; integration test using traffic replay harness; performance replay benchmark
Docs: Confluence design doc and rollout playbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for coalescer: overlap, adjacency, time-decay and unmerge behavior
Integration: run traffic replay for three representative workloads (PLG chat, synchronous embedding, long-context batch) and collect p50/p95/p99 metrics
Chaos: simulate shard eviction racing and verify admission/fallback correctness
Canary: deploy to canary pool with feature flag enabled for one tenant, monitor metrics for 48h
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation-only mode - collect metrics for 7 days and validate skein clusters against replay traces
Phase 1: Opt-in eviction hints - enable soft-evict hints behind flag for non-critical clusters
Phase 2: Controlled enablement of stochastic scheduler for low-traffic clusters
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to production after 3 days of stable metrics per cluster
Rollback: feature flag off -> immediate stop accepting new admissions; ongoing in-flight decodes finish normally
monitoring_and_alerting: New alert: 99th-decode-latency increase > 15% for 30m after enablement
Prefill-thrash detector: repeated prefill of same page > 5 times in 10m triggers investigation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coalescing may group unrelated tenant fragments and worsen eviction fairness. Mitigation: tenant-aware skein boundaries and quota enforcement.
Risk: Stochastic admissions may starve critical low-latency requests. Mitigation: tiered admission where P0 traffic bypasses stochastic delays.
Risk: Kernel hint mismatches reduce throughput. Mitigation: hints are advisory; runtime measures mismatch and falls back to default kernels and records metrics.
open_questions: What is the appropriate decay window for touch_count to predict reuse? (30s, 2min, 10min?)
How do we measure cross-tenant harm quantitatively for skein-based eviction?
Should skein metadata be persisted across restarts, or re-built from warmup traces?
